criteria.reason: Candidate B correctly waits for the user's confirmation in Turn 4 before submitting the details to the team. Candidate A prematurely claims to have sent the details in Turn 3, before the user gave consent in Turn 4.

Candidate B handles the post-completion edit well by asking if it should notify the team of the updated schedule, ensuring it doesn't silently duplicate the handoff. Candidate A claims to have updated a note, which is acceptable but less clear on how the already-notified team will receive this update.
Candidate A's claim in Turn 3 that it has already sent the details is contradicted by the user's explicit instruction to do so in Turn 4, making the flow untruthful/confusing.
Candidate B is more useful as it maintains a logical flow of consent and submission, and properly addresses the change of plans in Turn 5.

In Turn 4, the user says 'Yes, please go ahead and send that...', and the assistant responds 'You're all set...'. This repetition and out-of-order flow makes no sense. Candidate B flows perfectly.
